purpose:
Documents are released without a document class today. Downstream consumers cannot filter or route them.

This concept introduces a mandatory document class, checked before release.

objectives.title: Complete classification
points: Every released Document Revision carries a document class.

objectives.title: No manual rework
points: Missing classes are caught before the release workflow starts.

business_context: Document Revisions are released through the standard release workflow in Teamcenter.

challenges.title: Unclassified releases
challenges.text: About 30% of released documents carry no class.

in.heading: Data Model
items: New LOV-backed property on Document Revision

in.heading: Workflow
items: Release blocked when the class is empty

out.heading: Migration
items: Classification of already released documents (separate concept)

use_cases.title: Release a classified document
use_cases.trigger: User submits a Document Revision to the release workflow
use_cases.narrative: The user sets the document class in Active Workspace and starts the release workflow. The workflow checks the class before the first review task.
rules: Class must be a value of the document class LOV.
Released revisions cannot change their class.

ui.summary: One new mandatory field on the Document Revision summary page.
current: Users release documents without setting a class.
target: Users pick a class from a dropdown before release.
impact: One extra field to fill per document.
support: AWC stylesheet change for the summary and create panels.
ui.validation: If the class is empty when the workflow starts, the workflow is not started and the user sees the error message defined in the technical concept.

assumptions: The LOV values are owned and maintained by Document Control.
LOV changes need a BMIDE deployment per change.
risks: Users pick a wrong class to pass the check
Training, periodic report on class distribution

functional: Release workflow refuses a Document Revision without class.
user: Class field is visible on summary and create panels.

technical.intro: The class is a BMIDE property with a static LOV. A workflow rule handler checks it at release start. AWC shows it through a stylesheet change.

architecture.text: Three building blocks, no custom server code beyond one rule handler.

technical.workflow:
- Template: release workflow, root task `start` event.
- Rule handler `EPM-check-object-properties` on `x4_doc_class`.
- Error behavior: block.
